om.what: Organic matter comes from plants, animals and soil organisms.
om.changes: Its amount affects how soil holds water and nutrients.
om.effect: Soil structure and moisture affect leafy vegetable roots.

n.what: Nitrogen is a nutrient, and the report identifies which form was measured.
n.changes: A higher reading means more of the measured form. The test method and sampling time matter.
n.effect: Nitrogen is involved in leaf growth.

p.what: Phosphorus is a nutrient involved in moving energy within plants.
p.changes: A higher or lower reading reflects phosphorus measured by the stated method.
p.effect: Root and new leaf growth depend on phosphorus.

k.what: Potassium is a nutrient plants use to regulate water.
k.changes: A higher reading shows more measured potassium. Availability also depends on the soil.
k.effect: Potassium helps regulate water within leaves.

caco3.what: Calcium carbonate is a mineral found in calcareous soils.
caco3.changes: More carbonate often makes soil resist changes in acidity.
caco3.effect: In calcareous soil some nutrients may be less available to roots.

sodium.what: Sodium is one of the dissolved elements measured in water and soil.
sodium.changes: A higher reading shows more sodium in the form measured.
sodium.effect: Sodium buildup can affect how water reaches the roots.

sar.what: The sodium adsorption ratio compares sodium with calcium and magnesium in water.
sar.changes: A higher ratio means more sodium relative to those other elements.
sar.effect: In some soils the ratio affects how readily water moves toward the roots.

cl.what: Chloride is a dissolved ion found in water and soil.
cl.changes: A higher reading means more chloride in the sample.
cl.effect: Buildup can affect the leaves of some crops.

no3.what: Nitrate is a dissolved form of nitrogen.
no3.changes: The reading varies with water, soil and the time of sampling.
no3.effect: Leafy crops use nitrate for growth. A soil or water result cannot show nitrate in the leaves.

ec.what: Electrical conductivity shows how readily water conducts electricity.
ec.changes: With the same method, a higher reading generally indicates more dissolved salts.
ec.effect: More salts around the roots can make it harder for plants to take up water.

ph.what: pH indicates how acidic or alkaline the water is.
ph.changes: Lower readings are more acidic. Higher readings are more alkaline.
ph.effect: Acidity around roots affects how available nutrients are.
